description: Fixed false-completion sentinel set. Each 'reject' case is a trap the Kernel must NOT accept; 'accept' controls verify the harness is not trivially blocking everything, and that the legitimate end-to-end paths (bootstrap, resume, non-Node proof, sequential CLI processes) still complete.

cases.rationale: Source mutated but only caller-attested proof supplied; needs kernel-runtime hard evidence.
Verification passed, then source mutated again; evidence is stale.
A required obligation was never satisfied.
Acceptance criterion has no covering evidence.
Mutating run closed with no verification at all.
Protected obligation (auth) waived instead of proven.
The only evidence is a failing verification.
A trivially-passing script filed under typed obligation names; the command binding must reject it.
Structured judgments cannot satisfy executable obligations.
One trivial hard proof plus judgments for every other obligation must not complete a T3 run.
Accepted completion with failed finalization must not be reported as done.
A requested but unenforceable network sandbox must block rather than record isolation.
An evidence plan named a no-op script as hard proof; plan commands face the same classification check as policy obligations.
A shorter later contract replaces the active acceptance authority, permits removal of the old criterion, and keeps the same Run.
A protected T3 judgment submitted without an implementer identity must not skip the independence check.
A finalization retry must not turn an unfinished Git closeout into a clean completion by losing the selected paths.
A protected T3 judgment naming a second reviewer string, with no Review Receipt behind it, must not satisfy the obligation.
An execution capsule built before the workspace moved describes a state that no longer exists and cannot be reported against.
A change outside the work unit scope is a plan change; the report is refused before any evidence runs.
A report naming a step that is not the current work unit must not advance the cursor.
Legitimate: mutating run with passing kernel-runtime hard evidence and covered acceptance.
Legitimate: a run resumed in a fresh control plane keeps its constraints and non-goals and can still complete.
Legitimate: consecutive CLI-style processes must not deadlock on an abandoned lease.
Legitimate: a Makefile-declared command is provable without a package.json script.
Legitimate: the host bootstraps the run idempotently; the model never calls a start command.
